newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond trade slow amid uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond trade slow amid uncertainty.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond markets experienced a day of lackluster trading on Friday, following the release of a series of economic and technical numbers that offered mixed messages to the market, traders said.

The high-yield market breathed a sigh of relief as AMG Data Service reported $143 million in new cash poured into junk bond mutual funds in the latest week surveyed. Many in the market had expected to see net outflows.
Yet the inflows were also the lowest since the end of last year and represented a significant drop from the previous week's levels of $527 million.

Returning to the high-yield market, traders said the better bids returned to the zero coupon bonds of several competitive local exchange carriers (CLECs) after fears of an overhang in new supply had begun to fade.
In the past two days, two such carriers, Hyperion Telecommunications and Teleport Communications Group, postponed upcoming debt offerings due to market conditions.

Teleport's announcement this morning pushed bids on the company's outstanding bonds up one and one-half points, traders said. Bids on the bonds of Brooks Fiber Properties also rose three-quarters of a point on the news.
